## Early life

Headlam was born in St Helens, Lismore, then in the colony of New South Wales. He later moved with his family to the Hawkesbury River district near Windsor. Headlam, like his brothers, gained a scholarship to Sydney Grammar School.^{ [2] } After leaving school, he joined his brothers in the employment of the government lands office.

## Naval service

After a time as a junior clerk, Headlam's health deteriorated, due to a malarial condition caused by work on swamps. He was advised to go to sea, and, as a temporary measure, joined the staff of the Lands Office ship, the Lady Nelson. Antebellum period but the city is also an architectural time capsule as well. The city is home to multiple houses dating from the Antebellum period, the Civil war era, to the turn of the century.

The St. James Episcopal Church is one of those time capsules as the original structure dates back to 1853. The church is still an active Episcopal Church, serving the Episcopal Parish of Meridian. The church also hosts a community center that is available for rent. Please see the "Rentals" tab above for more information on center services.

The church building was designed by John L. Nussett, an architect who is best known for his work in the Diocese of Mississippi. Other Nussett designs include the diocesan cathedrals in both Natchez and Vicksburg; Holy Trinity Episcopal Church in Port Gibson and the St. Stephens Episcopal Church in Greenville, Mississippi. The church building was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973, as part of the Meridian National Register Historic district.

The 7th Division was sent east and began arriving on 1 February, just in time to halt the main Australian landing at the Munda Airstrip the following week.

Chak Tok Ich 'aak was the son of the twelfth king of Tikal, Jasaw Ch'an K'awiil, and was the grandson of the tenth king, K'inich Janaab' Pakal. He began his reign under the regnal number (4.11.0.0.0) 9 Ahaw 1 Zip, and his successor was Yik'in Ch'an K'awiil.

Chak Tok Ich 'aak's name translates as "Ruler (Chak) of Jaguar (Tok) Tail (Ich)"; or "Lord of (Chak) Jaguar's Feathered (Tok) Tail (Ich)". His name contains the word Tok, which is associated with the jaguar, and the word Ich, which is associated with the tail. His name contains the name of a prominent mythological hero named Ch'aak Tok, who is said to be the god of lightning. Chak Tok Ich 'aak's name may suggest

The stela was erected in Tikal by Yax Pasaj , the ruler of Tikal, during a trip he made to Caracol between 573 and 593 C.E.

By the start of the 8th century, however, Caracol had emerged as a regional superpower, eventually rivaling Tikal in prestige. Caracol's power was primarily military in nature, and it controlled a large region, including parts of Mexico.
